purpose: Defines non-node knowledge assets such as expert cohorts, experimental protocols, operating institutions, and manufacturing know-how. These assets help explain why possessing blueprints or a captured device is not equivalent to being able to reproduce alien technology.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Codified Scientific Records
knowledge_asset_types.description: Papers, models, blueprints, equations, documentation, and formal records. Highly transferable but often incomplete for difficult engineering.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Experimental Dataset
knowledge_asset_types.description: Measurements, calibration data, failure records, and reproducibility evidence.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Experimental Protocols
knowledge_asset_types.description: Procedures, calibration practice, preparation steps, and laboratory methods that are more operational than published theory.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Intact Prototype or Device
knowledge_asset_types.description: A functioning or substantially intact example that proves implementation details but may still be impossible to reproduce.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Manufacturing Tooling & Process Chain
knowledge_asset_types.description: Specialized tooling, process parameters, quality-control methods, precursor preparation, and production fixtures.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Expert Cohort
knowledge_asset_types.description: An aggregated group of scientists, engineers, technicians, or operators carrying experience that is difficult to fully encode. Do not simulate one research object per person.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Operating Scientific/Industrial Institution
knowledge_asset_types.description: A functioning laboratory, shipyard, biological culture system, alien factory, or other institution whose routines embody practical knowledge.

knowledge_asset_types.name: Training & Apprenticeship Pipeline
knowledge_asset_types.description: Education, apprenticeships, certification, simulation, and mentoring that reproduce expertise across generations.

asset_scope.rule: An asset only supports the scope it actually contains; an expert in alien propulsion does not become a universal alien-technology bonus.

research_rules: Foreign experts can improve tacit-expertise readiness for relevant fields/nodes but do not instantly grant mature technology.
An intact foreign factory plus its specialists may allow operation before the holder can reproduce the technology natively.
Removing/killing/losing the specialist cohort can reduce operating or reproduction ability if knowledge has not been codified/trained locally.
Translation, biological compatibility, security/trust, and available facilities can limit how much expertise is usable.
Coercion can provide access to people/equipment but does not guarantee truthful cooperation or complete transfer; diplomacy/internal-politics systems own those consequences.

assimilation_progression.meaning: Civilization possesses or can consult the asset, but knowledge remains externally dependent.
Enough language/context exists to use the asset in relevant research.
A meaningful portion of tacit knowledge has been converted into local records/procedures.
Local institutions can reproduce expertise through a training pipeline.
The civilization has internalized the knowledge sufficiently that loss of the original foreign asset no longer removes the competence.

project_readiness_interface.hard_requirement_possible: Some explicit projects may require a relevant operating process/expert asset before Engineering can proceed, particularly foreign or biologically alien technology.
